message.content: Our vets lose things between the morning and evening shift — a dog that needed re-checking, an owner who was promised a call back. Everyone blames the whiteboard but I don't think the whiteboard is the problem.

Agreed that the whiteboard is probably a symptom. Three things worth pulling apart: what specifically falls through, who is meant to be carrying it at the moment it falls, and only then what shape a fix would take.
The call-backs are the ones that sting. A missed re-check we catch the next day. A missed call-back we hear about in a review.

description: The only saved board that exercises what a card can actually CARRY. Three lines of thinking of unequal length — three cards, two, then four — so the conclusion has to clear the longest run rather than a typical one. One card holds a photograph and one a drawn shape, both at the wide width that pushes their neighbours along instead of overlapping them; two open questions carry the partner's shortlist with the way past it underneath. Every other saved board is plain text, which is why the card that silently dropped its diagram went unseen for a whole build.
